name: Chang'e 2
first: China's second lunar orbiter, later sent on to Sun-Earth L2 and the asteroid Toutatis
description: Chang'e 2 launched from Xichang on 2010-10-01 on a Long March 3C and entered lunar orbit on 2010-10-06; its 100 km working orbit followed on 2010-10-09, and its perilune was lowered to 15 km late in the mission. China published lunar images from it with a resolution of up to 1.3 m. On 2011-06-08 it left lunar orbit, reached the Sun-Earth L2 point on 2011-08-25 and left it on 2012-04-15 to fly by the asteroid 4179 Toutatis on 2012-12-13, imaging it at up to 10 m per pixel; the closest approach is reported as 3.2 km. It was built on the DFH-3 satellite bus.
